solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heads intense bombardment, having taken cannabis back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the bombardment word followed by the drug word from right to left

parts.note: a stonk is military slang for a concentrated artillery bombardment
pot is a slang name for cannabis

explanation.surface: A soldier under heavy shellfire has been smoking dope to cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' suggests skulls or leaders; it means hair tied up on the crown. 'back' turns the whole of STONKPOT round.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairdressing sense: tufts or buns of hair worn on the crown, plural like 'Heads'.

clue.text: A woman of the night looking up a port in Oklahoma

indicators.note: looking up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a crude term for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: A streetwalker gazing up at an American river city.
explanation.walkthrough: Tulsa is an inland port on the Arkansas River navigation system.
explanation.definitionFit: This Oklahoma city has a river port, the Port of Catoosa, linked to the Mississippi.

clue.text: Gene type in flux

indicators.note: in flux means in a state of change, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A genetics remark about a gene variant that keeps mutating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gene' is the singer Gene Pitney, not biology; 'in' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene is the first name of the American singer of 'Town Without Pity'.

clue.text: Add anything to pieces to get a song

indicators.note: breaking something to pieces means scattering its parts, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A songwriter tinkering by adding odd bits to fragments until a tune emerges.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter's 1932 standard, sung by Fred Astaire in The Gay Divorcee.

clue.text: Probably it's a wrench for 'handy' man having nothing left to fight about

definitions.text: Probably it's a wrench for 'handy' man

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
to box about is to spar or fight around the ring

explanation.surface: A DIY enthusiast with no spanner left squares up for a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is 'it has': a wrench is probably inside one. 'having' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool kit's case, which a DIY handyman uses to store spanners and screwdrivers.

clue.text: Odd snatches of sketch, Cook being dry

indicators.note: odd snatches means taking the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the following words

explanation.surface: A comic sketch about a cook whose humour is very dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Italian wine term, borrowed into English for dry wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian label word for wine that is not sweet, as in a dry Lambrusco.

clue.text: A shocking report issued on aircraft

definitions.text: A shocking report issued on aircraft

parts.words: A shocking report issued on aircraft
parts.note: read as scandalous news about planes, it is the bang from a shock wave

explanation.surface: A scandalous news story published about aeroplanes.
explanation.definitionFit: The loud explosive bang made by a shock wave from a plane flying faster than sound.

clue.text: A cut of fish that was 'outstanding' in the area for members?

definitions.text: that was 'outstanding' in the area for members?

parts.note: cod is a common food fish
a piece is a cut or portion

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's portion, prized by club members.
explanation.walkthrough: The innuendo: 'members' and 'outstanding' are bawdy, as was this Tudor garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouch worn at the front of men's hose in Tudor times, prominent over the groin.

clue.text: Axes soldiers following order in operation to capture figure during speech

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the soldiers come after the honour
to capture means to hold inside, so the honour encloses the axes

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
x and y are the axes of a graph
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
on means working, in operation

explanation.surface: Troops marching to orders during an operation to seize a speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure during speech' stands for figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorical device pairing contradictory terms, like 'deafening silence', a classic figure of speech.

clue.text: Shall we mismanage releases?

definitions.meaning: a suggestion to bungle together: 'let us goof'
unhands or stops holding, as in letting go of a rope

explanation.surface: A manager wonders whether to botch the press releases.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase read two ways: LET'S GOOF + OF, and LETS GO OF.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go of something is to release it; goof is slang for blunder.

clue.text: See 3
The composer is somewhat flabbergasted

indicators.note: somewhat means only a part, so the name lies within the long word

explanation.surface: A composer left a little astonished.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was the Austrian composer of the opera Wozzeck.

clue.text: Beat liver troubles that could have been prevented

indicators.note: troubles means disturbs, so the letters of the two words before it are stirred up

explanation.surface: Cirrhosis or a battered liver from drinking is self-inflicted harm that need never have happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Something avoidable could be turned aside or warded off before it happened.

clue.text: One of the 13 17, I've had too much to drink in company

indicators.note: in tells us the drunk's noise sits inside the company abbreviation

parts.words: I've had too much to drink
parts.note: a hiccup, written hic, is the comic sign of drunkenness

explanation.surface: A tipsy guest at a party admits to overdoing it while among friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Chico, Harpo, Groucho (and Zeppo, Gummo) were the comedy siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: Chico was the piano-playing, fake-Italian member of the family comedy act.

clue.text: Damage by old trains et al, they spent 3 9 at 29 and 27

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
X as in multiplication: two by four is two x four
BR is British Rail, the former UK state railway
Latin et alii, 'and others'

explanation.surface: Vandals wrecking vintage rolling stock, plus a list of others involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 9 is NIGHT AND DAY, 29 THE OPERA and 27 THE RACES: their films A Night at the Opera and A Day at the Races.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedy family starred in A Night at the Opera (1935) and A Day at the Races (1937).

clue.text: They quickly shot off a letter in Athens, sent both ways containing no news

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: containing no means the named letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written, the first, forward copy

indicators.note: both ways means the word is written forwards then backwards

parts.note: taken as written, the second copy, which is turned round
N stands for new, so news is a pair of Ns

explanation.surface: A letter sent from Greece, going both ways, carried no fresh information.
explanation.walkthrough: SENT + TNES, less both Ns, leaves SETTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusettes were light rapid-fire field guns of the 18th century.

clue.text: One of the 13 17, one easily-annoyed all-rounder

parts.note: a grouch is a grumpy, irritable person
O is round, so it can stand for anything round

explanation.surface: A cricketer who bowls and bats but has a short temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all-rounder' looks like a cricketer (one good at batting and bowling); here it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho, with greasepaint moustache and cigar, was the wisecracking leader of the comedy siblings.

clue.text: Cupid's dart finally penetrating Romeo at livery

definitions.note: Cupid's is read as 'Cupid is', so the definition is Cupid

indicators.note: penetrating means going into, so the dart's final letter enters the rearranged pair
livery here means liverish, out of sorts, so the letters are disordered
finally picks the closing letter of dart

explanation.surface: Cupid's arrow finally pierces a Romeo at a livery company dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'livery' is read as liverish, i.e. upset.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a little cupid figure, a cherub of love in Italian art.

clue.text: See 13
Rising with the sun, it is one who spent 3 9 at 29 and 27

definitions.text: Rising with the sun, it is
definitions.meaning: the innermost planet, never far from the sun, rises with it
Freddie, Queen's singer, whose albums were A Night at the Opera and A Day at the Races

explanation.surface: An early riser who passed his days and nights at the theatre and the track.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen named two albums after the comedy siblings' films, so their frontman 'spent' night and day there.
explanation.definitionFit: Planet nearest the sun; also Freddie, the Queen frontman, on whose albums those titles appear.

clue.text: A little horribly affected Scotsman's scold

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Scot giving someone a mildly theatrical telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots dialect verb for barking, yelping or nagging at someone.

clue.text: Adult backing online celebrity

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for adult is written backwards

parts.note: a man is an adult male
E for electronic, as in e-mail, means online

explanation.surface: A grown-up endorses an internet star.
explanation.definitionFit: A big name is a celebrity, a famous person everyone has heard of.

clue.text: Lowest-of-the-low ordinal should, in New Hampshire

indicators.note: in places the word for should inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: NH is the postal abbreviation for the US state
ought means should

explanation.surface: A New England state is being urged towards bottom place.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal for zero, coming before first, so the lowest possible position.

clue.text: Not the last living male to prepare a cheese flan

indicators.note: not the last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: quick means alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man who has not been the final survivor makes a cheesy tart.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury tart of eggs and cheese baked in pastry, from Lorraine.

clue.text: Take another bow on appearing before cup match

indicators.note: appearing before puts the word for 'on' in front of the match word

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a tie is a knockout match in a cup competition

explanation.surface: A performer takes a second curtain call ahead of a football cup game.
explanation.walkthrough: The bow is a knot, not a gesture to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie a bow again, fastening a knot a second time.

clue.text: See 26
One of the 13 17 reviving the Confessor?

indicators.note: read as re-viving, revived backwards, so the talk-show name is reversed

parts.note: Oprah Winfrey's TV show was famous for guests' confessions

explanation.surface: Bringing Edward the Confessor back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Confessor' suggests Edward the Confessor, the English king; it is the talk-show host.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpo, the silent harp-playing brother with a horn, was part of the comedy family.

clue.text: Fools growing up? Enough said!

indicators.note: growing up in a down clue means the letters climb from bottom to top

parts.note: asses are fools

explanation.surface: A weary remark about idiots who finally mature.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespearean interjection (Taming of the Shrew): 'be quiet, let it go'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation meaning 'say no more', used by Christopher Sly.

clue.text: For 2 it's time to go to 1 down or 3 9

definitions.text: For 2 it's time to go to 1 down
definitions.meaning: Gene Pitney's song is titled with this span 'from Tulsa'
night and day together make a full day's span of time

explanation.surface: A man's travel plans to an Oklahoma city, or the length of a whole day.
explanation.walkthrough: Gene Pitney (2) sang 'Twenty Four Hours from Tulsa' (1 down) in 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: A full day, both its night and its daylight, lasts this length of time.

clue.text: With run in plus hard going it would be where fans would watch sporting event

indicators.note: plus here adds a letter into the stand word to make the event
in reads backwards: the event with run added would be the stand, so that letter comes out of the stand

parts.note: terraces are the standing areas of a football ground
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A long horse race on a firm track and the stands where spectators gather.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer with R in and H going would become TERRACES; so take R out of TERRACES and put H in.
explanation.definitionFit: A day's horse racing meeting is a sporting event, a fixture at a course.

clue.text: So Status Quo getting behind old band?

indicators.note: getting behind means coming after, so the status quo phrase follows the letter for old

parts.note: the status quo is the way things are, as is

explanation.surface: The rock group Status Quo backing an older band.
explanation.walkthrough: Status Quo and Oasis are both British rock bands, which hides the Latin sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gallagher brothers' Manchester group was a famous Britpop band of the 1990s.

clue.text: It's a job for surgeon in makeshift theatre — no time for dramas

indicators.note: in places the surgeon's job inside the rearranged letters
makeshift means improvised, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order
no tells us the time letter is dropped from the theatre word

parts.note: an op, short for operation, is a surgeon's work

explanation.surface: A surgeon working in a makeshift operating theatre has no time for histrionics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' looks like the operating theatre but is the fodder: 'no' drops a T and 'makeshift' rearranges the rest into THEERA, opened round the surgeon's job.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera as a genre is drama set to music; the Latin plural sense also means works.
